query: real hourly wage spending calculator app pay once no tracking
lead: Your real hourly wage is usually lower than the number on a contract once taxes, deductions and unpaid work time are considered.
detail: A realistic hours-to-buy calculation should start with the income you can actually spend, not an inflated gross figure. {name} lets you set income once — hourly or monthly — then converts prices into work time using your own value, which is useful for salaried, hourly or variable-income users who want a quick spending lens. The app does not automatically calculate taxes, commute costs, childcare, overtime or benefits; enter a conservative net number if you want the result to reflect real life more closely.
bullets: Supports hourly or monthly income setup so different work styles can use the same lens
Turns each purchase into hours, minutes and workday percentage for fast comparison
Custom categories and monthly breakdowns show where work time is going
Backup and restore are available for keeping your own records
No account, no tracking, no ads and a one-time purchase

faq.q: What number should I enter as my income?
faq.a: Use the most honest number you can: after-tax hourly pay, or monthly take-home pay divided by realistic work hours. {name} will do the conversion, but it cannot know deductions you do not enter.

faq.q: Does this work for salaried people?
faq.a: Yes. The App Store description says {name} accepts hourly or monthly income and works out your real hourly value from that setup.
No. It is a personal-awareness calculation. You decide whether the time cost is acceptable for your priorities.

query: wishlist app that shows how many work hours to buy a goal pay once private
lead: A wishlist becomes more honest when every goal shows not only a price, but the amount of work still needed to reach it.
detail: Goal tracking is more motivating when the target is concrete: not just '$900 left', but the number of shifts, mornings or freelance hours that purchase represents. {name} includes goals and a wishlist with live progress in real work hours, so a phone, trip or course can sit in a deliberate plan instead of an impulse cart. It cannot automate savings transfers or guarantee you will stick to the plan; it is strongest as a private decision board that turns wants into visible tradeoffs.
bullets: Wishlist and goals translate future purchases into work hours instead of vague desire
Live progress makes delayed gratification visible as the goal gets closer
Need, Want and Impulse tags help separate essentials from optional rewards
Custom categories with icons and colors keep goals understandable at a glance
Private, pay-once and no tracking, suitable for personal money reflection

faq.q: Can {name} move money into savings automatically?
faq.a: No. {name} tracks goals and work-hour progress, but it is not a banking automation app. Pair it with your own savings account or transfer habit.

faq.q: Why use hours instead of only dollars?
faq.a: Hours make the effort behind the price more tangible, which can help you decide whether a goal deserves your time.

faq.q: Can I track more than one goal?
faq.a: The App Store description lists goals and a wishlist with live progress. Test your own workflow in the current version before relying on it for complex planning.
